docs.title: Andor's Trail Wiki
docs.text:
An always-current reference for Andor's Trail, generated straight from the game's own open-source data. This wiki currently describes v0.8.18, the latest release, and rebuilds itself automatically when a new version is tagged.

  • Items1005 items, with stats and drop sources
  • Monsters1907 monsters and NPCs, with drops and locations
  • Skills45 skills, with requirements
  • Quests151 quests and their journal stages
  • Maps1207 maps with spawns
  • ChangelogWhat changed in each release

Game data © the Andor's Trail contributors, used under the project's open-source licenses. This is an unofficial fan wiki.

Foundation of the Forgotten Kingdom (year 2300) The first humans, led by Arntuk the Mighty, came from the south in ancient times and established the Forgotten Kingdom. These people, called the Lethgar, built settlements in places where now great towns and cities are located. Nor City and Sullengard were the first to be founded. Then some time later, a few explorers climbed Mount Galmore, the highest mountain in Dhayavar. Due to the elevation and marvelous view, their priests and mages built a sanctuary near the summit where they studied the arts of magic and worshipped their gods.

Rise of Kazaul (year 2177) The insane and powerful wizard called Valugha was obsessed with the notion of creating a portal to another plane. Even though his fellow mages disapproved, he was able to create a portal by consuming the powerful life essence of his brothers and the stored energy in the sanctuary. The sanctuary erupted in an explosion and a large ravine split Mt. Galmore apart. At its bottom, the portal opened, which was soon merely called the 'Rift', and the devastated area around it 'Undertell'. The mountain also spilled out lava like blood coming from a wound and is now clouded in smoke all the time. All kinds of demons and undead emerged into the world through the portal, led by their masters, the 'Kazaul'. The Kazaul themselves were guided by the Eternal Masters who were incredibly skilled in magic and warcraft. Soon the monsters and their masters spread over whole of Dhayavar. However, the portal became unstable after a while and finally collapsed after several decades, but the harm was already done, as thousands of beasts had crept through it into the realm. A short and brutal war was fought. With the loss of nearly all mages, the Lethgar were powerless against the monster invasion and were soon overthrown and enslaved by the Kazaul. The Kazaul imposed a reign of terror on the Forgotten Kingdom. It seemed no one was able to defeat or oppose the Kazaul due to their inhuman strength. Then the Lethgar had to build underground lairs for their oppressors. A large city was built around the deactivated portal and in the natural caves under Mt. Galmore. Also, Carn Tower and the Sanctuary on Blackwater Mountain were built, among countless other underground Kazaul settlements. Even though most Lethgar despised their masters, some showed interest in the rituals and dark sorcery of the Kazaul. As a result, the Kha'zaan (Kazaul cultists), a group of human Kazaul followers, gathered around their masters and learned from them. They were often used to enforce the brutal rule of the Kazaul. Many of the current monsters are living forms that evolved from experiments made during this era, such as Izthiels, Gornauds, Wyrms, etc. By that time, the Hira'zinn, the omen of war, started plaguing the smallfolk.

The War of Dawn and the Rise of Elythara and the Elytharan Union (year 1537) One day, the Elytharan cultists arrived on the shore of the northern sea (Sea of Tears). They worshipped the blinding and cleansing light of Elythara. The Elytharan mages and warriors were able to defeat the Kazaul and Kha'zaan with the help of the blinding light of Elythara which was forged

[... here some pages were torn out ...]

began erecting the city of Feygard on the shore of the Sea of Tears, which soon became a center of trade for the realm due to its access to the sea. The town of Loneford was founded and it soon became famous for its fertile fields and healthy vegetable which fed the northern parts of the Forgotten Kingdom. Blackwater Mountain was explored, and on its summit a large sanctuary for the Elytharan priests was erected to study dawn and dusk, the sun and stars, and to watch over the Forgotten Kingdom. Other sanctuaries were located in Feygard and Nor City, and shrines were found in each minor settlement. The mining colony of Prim was also founded after pioneers found rich sources of iron and coal under the mountain. The city of Fallhaven became a prosperous center of trade due to its excellent location as a junction between the sanctuary of Blackwater Mountain, Stoutford, Nor City and Feygard. Big storehouses were built to safely store shipments. However, bands of thieves were soon attracted by the growing wealth, and united under one big organization, the Thieves' Guild, whose guild halls were secretly placed in Fallhaven, Feygard, and Nor City, those being the richest cities at that time. Many other towns, including Brimhaven and Brightport were also founded around this time, and the Charwood mines were opened. Trade agreements were signed between the cities in order to make trade prosper further.

Establishment of the Aewatha Kingdom (year 432) The head of the most important Nor City family, Garthan I of house Houdart, declared himself King, marking the end of the Elytharan era and the beginning of the Shadow-supported kingdom. At this point, political power and religious power became closely united. As the kingdom prospered, so did the Shadow, and Elythara

[... again some pages were torn out ...]

as slaves for the digging. At that time the Flagstone Prison was also built, where runaway workers from Mt. Galmore were imprisoned and were left to rot. However the mines were closed after some years due to frequent monster attacks and other unspeakable horrors who dwelt in the dark. Remgard was founded by Korhald of Remgard and built on a large island in Lake Laeroth. It became famous for its excellent smithing services. The village of Crossglen was founded, and farmers settled there. King Luthor ascended to the throne as the direct heir of King Oromir III and moved the capital from Nor City to Fallhaven, while the center of worship remained in Nor City. As King Luthor got older he felt the need for an advisor, and so Lord Geomyr of Feygard was named Hand of the King. He fulfilled his duty with great obsession and effort.

The Noble Wars (year 25 to 14) When King Luthor died, he left the Kingdom with no heir to the throne. He was buried in the catacombs under Fallhaven church. What followed, the Noble Wars, was one of the darkest periods this country has witnessed. Four coalitions were formed which were each ruled by one powerful Lord. The Western one consisted of Stoutford and the settlements on Blackwater Mountain, and was ruled by Lord Erwyn. The Northern one consisted of Feygard, Thalgard, Luthaven and Remgard, and was ruled by Lord Geomyr. The Eastern one consisted of Nor City, Sullengard, Brightport and Brimhaven, and was ruled by Lord Emeric. The center capital area at first remained neutral and consisted of Fallhaven, Vilegard and Loneford (formerly administrated by King Luthor). The Noble Wars started with the Landlords arguing about who was to be the new, legitimate, King. The first stone was thrown by Stoutford. Lord Erwyn tried to use the time to attack the center area when the other Lords were busy debating. He wanted to occupy those to control the trade routes to Nor City, to gain the largest influence and to fracture other coalitions. Fallhaven was partially destroyed. Erwyn's success was a short one, as he was attacked by the Eastern coalition. For several years, numerous battles and countless skirmishes were fought over control of the center area. When both Lords were weakened, Lord Geomyr attacked and forced both to surrender. The peace treaty of Fallhaven was signed and Lord Geomyr was proclaimed King. The Hira'zinn haunted the lands once again during the war.

The Rule of King Geomyr (year 14) King Geomyr urged people to restore the destroyed cities and remove the traces of the long war. He reinstated a tax system, and garrisons of the Royal Guard of Feygard, in most of the villages. Geomyr promoted nepotism and corruption to further increase his power. The cult of the Shadow became ever more important for the smallfolk. The commoners felt the need for salvation after the harsh period of the Noble Wars and accepted the Shadow as their guide into better times. Lord Geomyr became fearful of the power of the religion, and tensions between Nor City and Feygard started to rise. He then proclaimed several prohibitions against the cult. They were no longer allowed to perform their rituals, and he tried to detain some of the priests. Then he even banned the trade and use of heartsteel weapons as he feared they would be used to overthrow him. He destroyed many weapons and confiscated others. Bonemeal potions were prohibited as well much to the disapproval of the smallfolk and the priests.

[... here the story ends - you can't tell if there had been more pages ...]

docs.title: The Noble Wars
docs.text:
Ordinary · Other · value 0 gold

In the year 57 of the rule of King luthor, the era of prosperity came to an end. Our king and hero, died. The lords, dukes, and nobles gathered in the capital of Fallhaven. To attend the funerary process of the king. At the time Fallhaven was a great city, extending it's reach much farther. Not long after, the nobility found themselves at an impasse, who would become the next ruler? King Luthor had left behind no known heir, and the opinions of the nobles shifted amongst themselves. One side pushed for Lord Erwin of House Garland as the new king, The ruler of Stoutford. Stoutford had long been the military center of the kingdom, experienced and hardened in their clashes with the uncivilized tribes of the western bogs and wildlands, as well as the occasional demonic incursions of Undertell. The warriors of Stoutford were a formidable force, the cornerstone of the kingdom's defense. Many nobles disagreed with House Garland ruling and instead favored Lord Emeric of House Houdart, the ruling house of Nor City which was the kingdom's historical capital and the center of culture and worship of the Shadow. The third faction rallied around Lord Geomyr of House Aumwill, the lord of Feygard and the former king's advisor. Lastly, a final faction was formed by the nobles of the central lands, who at first remained neutral, but fearing that a new king might threaten the status of Fallhaven as capital and shift it's importance away, chose to oppose the others. As discussions progressed, the four factions soon solidified into four coalitions. The Western Coalition, formed by Lord Erwin and his vassals, was centered around the town of Stoutford, along with it were the town of Prim and the settlement of Blackwater Mountain. The Central Coalition was formed by the various nobility and burghers of Crossglen, Loneford, Fallhaven, Vilegard, and Charwood. The Eastern Coalition was formed by the 3 great houses of Nor City with Lord Emeric of House Houdart in charge, along with other more minor nobility, especially those of Brimhaven and Brightport. And the clergy of Sullengard, who sought to return the king back to the historical center of Shadow worship. Lastly, the Northern Coalition, led by Lord Geomyr, was comprised of the city of Feygard, which housed the loathed cult of Elythara, as well as the mountain settlement of Thalgard and the town of Remgard. With this, the sides were set. As the discussions stalled, what was at first whispers turned to shouts of command. Lord Erwin rallied his troops to be the one first to move towards the central lands, the spies of the various factions rode their horses in a hurry to announce their overlords. By the time news reached the East, the Western troops were on the move. The western troops split in 3 and rallied in all directions. North, towards Loneford, south towards Sullengard, and northeast towards the capital. The 1st army had met no resistance taking Crossglen, and the occupation of the village was relatively peaceful until the end of the conflicts. In Fallhaven, the nobles, lacking central leadership, hurriedly mustered a militia force to man the palisades and resist the western coalition, having managed to do so just in time to offer resistance. Meanwhile, the 3rd army, moving south, struggled to cross the Sutdover River, delaying their advance on Sullengard. The houses of Nor City were caught off guard; no one had assumed the conflict would begin so soon after the discussions stalled. They rallied their troops, the bulk of their forces being comprised of commoners and numerous levies. The members of house Houdart led the army, with the trained knights of its branching houses forming the elite core of their forces. Orders were sent to the regional leadership, and the armies moved to meet with their allies. The 1st army was led by Lord Emeric of Imeria Houdart The 2nd army was led by Duke Vergas of Ryfarion Houdart, and the 3rd army was led by Baron Benzimos of Worgand Houdart. Ensuring the house of Houdart and it's branches would lead the Kingdom if they were to succeed. Lord Emeric moved his army towards Fallhaven right as the attack of the Western Coalition commenced, deceptive correspondence painted himself to the central nobles as reinforcements. Making the towns of Vilegard and Charwood join in with the eastern coalition. The second army merged with the troops of Brightport, while the third moved south to defend Sullengard. And so it commenced, the start of the First Noble War. The troops of the western coalition advanced to the crossroads fortification, capturing it with minor resistance. Scouts were sent south and north to gauge the other coalition's approach, as the bulk of the troops moved towards the defenseless Loneford. In the south, the Western forces had passed the river and were on the eastern bank, moving towards Sullengard. In the center, Stoutford's elite forces crushed the meager militia and forcefully assimilated the town guard into their ranks, just in time, as Lord Emeric and his troops approached from the east. The Battle of Fallhaven began. Bodies fell on each side. Stoutford's hardened elite barely held on against the numerous forces of Nor City. Fallhaven burned, its inhabitants forced to hide or flee. Its wealthier citizens had already escaped to Feygard, taking their possessions with them. In the south, the troops of the western coalition met with the forces of the eastern coalition, led by Baron Benzimos. The two armies clashed, and the Western Coalition was on its back foot. With their back against the river, they opted for a retreat. Hoping to form a defensive line at the bridge and defend Stoutford's southern flank. The leaders, whose names were lost to history, hastily pulled back, whilst suffering many casualties. the plan to capture Sullengard having failed. To the north, Stoutford's troops secured Loneford with ease. Scouts reported no movement from the northern coalition. Lord Emeric's central forces soon moved to contest the crossroads, leading to skirmishes along the Duleian Road. Meanwhile, the Eastern Coalition's army, led by Duke Vergas, wary of Feygard's movements, sent scouts north to assess the Northern Coalition's response as their forces moved to merge with Brimhaven's forces. This predicament continued for many years. Battles devolved into minor skirmishes as both coalitions avoided any decisive engagements, unwilling to risk the lives of their troops. Both sides camped outside the ever-burning ruins of Fallhaven. In the south, the Sutdover River became the dividing line, while in the north, skirmishes were taking place in the forest between Brimhaven and Loneford. The Northern Coalition having made no move. The prolonged stalemate created a false sense of security. The garrisons of the encampments set to protect the northern flanks of both coalitions steadily diminished as the main forces required reinforcements to replenish their ranks. An uneasy truce took hold, allowing each side time to recover for a decisive battle. The war exposed the strengths and weaknesses of both sides. The Eastern Coalition, backed by Nor City, wielded immense wealth and manpower but it was stretched thin, its forces spread too far apart. The Western Coalition could afford to fight the larger forces of the East due due to their position and their proximity to the coalition's center of power in Stoutford. Manpower being the only issue, but the West employed prisoners from the mines as footmen, with its elite group of warriors being able to turn a disadvantage of numbers into an equal fight. With this in mind, Lord Emeric devised a plan. He wanted to capture Fallhaven and secure the symbol of the king from the former king Luthor's grave. He would draw away Erwin's reinforcements in Fallhaven via an attack from the south and then attack the Western Coalition in Fallhaven. The period of the Second War commenced. The East reinforced its southern army led by Baron Benzimos, ordering him to attack the bridge and take it at all costs. This plan succeeded, leading to a panic in the center of the Western troops. The ruins of Fallhaven, now a smoldering ground far from its marble clad roads and opulent buildings. were contested by skirmishes nearly every day. The reinforcements from Stoutford and Blackwater allowed the Western coalition to hold its line, but the sudden advance from the south required that the supply of recruits was to focus on the Sutdover. Having moved according to the Eastern Coalition's plan, Lord Emeric rallied his troops. The Second Battle of Fallhaven commenced. Larger and more brutal than the first, having fought for months on end, both sides lost hundreds of troops. Lord Emeric's forces, having seemingly bested their enemies, started advancing towards the west. At that same time, the expected happened. The Third period of the Noble Warsb began. The troops of Feygard suddenly moved south from Feygard and Thalgard, crushing the minor garrisons set to defend against the north and moved to capture Loneford and Brimhaven. In Brimhaven, the leadership panicked and switched sides, leaving a portion of the Eastern troops led by Duke Vergas to follow Brimhaven in their rebellion and switch sides. The loyal to Nor City Vergas, fled along with the remaining of his troops to Brightport. Loneford was swiftly captured, and the advance of the northern coalition to Fallhaven was imminent. The Eastern Coalition was the first to disengage, with the forces of Baron Benzimos retreating to the stronghold of Sullengard. The remaining troops of Lord Emeric moved southeast on the Duleian. Lord Geomyr split his forces in two: one chased after Lord Emeric's army, while the other moved to capture the remains of Fallhaven. In Brightport, The Feygardian troops met the resistance hastily mounted by the remaining troops of Duke Vergas, and were successful in routing them, securing Brightport. Feygard captured Fallhaven and Crossglen, then moved toward Stoutford, where the western coalition prepared for a siege. Feygard's troops caught up to the fleeing troops of the Eastern coalition and dealt a devastating blow to the exhausted forces. Baron Benzimos left a small contingent to defend Sullengard and moved to assist his lord in the Battle of the now cursed forest. The Blackwater settlements were bribed to cut their support of the Western Coalition; their leaders were spared. The Feygardians, laid siege to Stoutford, capturing Lord Erwin and executing him, along with the surviving members of House Garland. The decisive battle between the troops of Feygard and the Eastern coalition, ended with Baron Benzimos recklessly charging into the ranks of armored Feygard knights. Leading to his demise. lord Emeric was killed by a stray arrow, and only a third of the troops returned to Nor City. House Welfort took control and signed a treaty with Feygard. Lord Geomyr was crowned king, marking the end of the war.

docs.title: Korhald Family Legacy
docs.text:
Rare · Other · value 0 gold

'In the annals of time,' [the text begins], 'there lived a man whose legend burns as brightly as the forge fires he tended. Korhald, master blacksmith and unmatched warrior, emerged from humble beginnings to etch his name upon the tapestry of fate.' [With each turn of the page, the tale unfolds before you like a parchment map unfurling across the expanse of memory.] 'Born of simple stock,' the words continue, 'Korhald inherited not only his father's name but also his legacy of hard work and unwavering resolve.' [As you delve deeper into the passages, you learn of Korhald's ascent from apprentice to artisan, his hands shaping steel with the precision of a sculptor and the strength of a titan.] 'In the heart of the forge,' the tome whispers, 'Korhald found not only his craft but also his calling, for his creations were not merely weapons and armor, but the very embodiment of his spirit.' [But Korhald's legacy extends beyond the anvil and the battlefield.] 'A leader among men,' the pages declare, 'Korhald's valor and wisdom guided his people through times of strife and uncertainty, laying the cornerstone upon which the town of Remgard would rise.'

[With each passing paragraph, you bear witness to the indomitable spirit of a man who forged his own destiny, shaping the world around him with the hammer blows of fate. And as you close the tome, the echoes of Korhald's journey linger in your mind, a testament to the enduring power of courage, determination, and the bonds of family that transcend the ages.]

docs.title: Booklet from Kealwea
docs.text:
Rare · Other · value 100 gold

'Thanks to $playername for preventing anything bad from happening. Kealwea, priest of Sullengard'

Of One Who Set Out to Learn to Be Fearful

Once upon a time, in a small, peaceful village, there lived a young boy named Emil. Emil was known for his courage and curiosity, but deep down, he often wondered if he truly knew nothing of fear. One day, he decided he wanted to learn to be afraid in order to become braver. So, he packed his things and set off into the dark forest surrounding the village.

The forest was full of mysterious sounds and shadows, but Emil bravely forged ahead. After a while, he came to an old, creaking bridge that led over a deep chasm. Suddenly, he heard a rustling in the bushes. A small fox leaped out, its eyes sparkling curiously. Emil was hardly startled, but the fox didn't seem afraid. Instead, it wagged its tail, seemingly inviting Emil to follow it. 'Well,' said Emil, 'if you're not afraid, then I won't be either.' He crossed the bridge, with the fox walking beside him. But no sooner had he crossed the bridge than Emil heard a loud growl. A large, dark wolf emerged from the bushes. Emil froze in shock. But the fox bravely stood in front of him and growled back. The wolf seemed surprised, hesitated for a moment, and then disappeared into the thicket.Emil was relieved, but he felt he still had more to learn.

He continued on his way and came to a cave that led deep into the mountain. Curious, he crept inside. It was dark and cool inside. Suddenly, he heard a faint cry. In the corner, he saw a small owl caught in a net. 'Oh, poor owl,' said Emil. 'I'll help you.' He carefully freed the small owl from the net. It looked at him gratefully and said, 'Thank you, brave Emil. You are not afraid of darkness and danger. That's very brave of you.' Emil felt proud, but at the same time, he realized that courage also means being kind and helpful.

On his way back to the village, Emil reflected. He had learned that fear isn't always a bad thing. Sometimes it's just fear that protects us from danger. But courage also means doing the right thing despite fear. When Emil finally arrived back in the village, everyone welcomed him. He told them about his adventures and what he had learned: that fear is part of life, but that you can be brave even when you're afraid. From that day on, Emil was not only curious, but also wiser and braver - ready to face every adventure with an open heart.

And if they didn't die, they're still afraid today. But they also know that courage is much stronger than any fear.

docs.title: Undertell: Its Ghosts and History
docs.text:
Quest · Other · value 0 gold

Undertell: Its Ghosts and History

Few places in Dhayavar inspire as much dread and fascination as the caverns beneath Mt. Galmore. Known collectively as Undertell, these depths have claimed the lives of miners, soldiers, scholars, and fortune-seekers alike.

What follows is a collected account of the known and suspected truths of Undertell, compiled from fragmented records, hearsay, and personal investigation.

Chapter I: The Mines Beneath the Mountain

It is beyond dispute that Undertell was once heavily mined. Gold veins, rare gems, and other valuable stones were extracted here for decades. Even now, abandoned tunnels and collapsed shafts bear unmistakable marks of pick and flame.

Though the mines were eventually sealed, it is widely believed that much wealth remains undisturbed in the deeper reaches. Fear, not scarcity, ended the mining operations.

Those brave or foolish enough to venture below still return with traces of gold, confirming that the mountain has not yet given up all it holds.

Chapter II: Miner's Sickness

Those who labored in the caverns beneath Undertell spoke of a sickness that came not from the air or the water, but from the stones themselves. At first, it was subtle. Miners complained of a bitter taste that lingered on the tongue after long hours in the tunnels. Their breath grew sour, and their sleep was broken by strange dreams of distant fires, of voices echoing through stone, of light burning behind closed eyes.

The sickness did not strike all who entered Undertell, only those who worked near the deeper seams, where the heartstone grew thickest in the rock. Those who merely passed through the caverns did not feel its touch. Those who lingered, who carved it free with bare hands and iron tools, carried something back with them when they returned to the surface. Not a curse.

Chapter III: On Ghosts and Lingering Spirits

Many claim Undertell is haunted. Travelers speak of pale figures watching from afar, whispers echoing through stone and shapes that vanish when approached.

Some insist these are the dead miners, bound by unfinished labor. Others claim the spirits are something older, drawn to the mountain long before any pick struck rock.

There is no agreement on whether these ghosts are hostile. Accounts vary wildly, some explorers report being ignored entirely, while others describe sudden violence without warning.

Chapter IV: The Lethgar and the Elytharans

Two distinct groups of spirits are frequently mentioned in surviving accounts.

The Lethgar are described as orderly, almost disciplined, haunting areas closest to the old mining routes. Some believe they were guards or overseers in life.

The Elytharans, by contrast, appear scattered and erratic. Their presence is strongest near collapsed tunnels and forgotten chambers. Whether they are miners, prisoners, or something else entirely remains unclear.

It is possible these distinctions are imagined by fearful minds seeking patterns where none exist.

Chapter V: Of Darkness and the Shadow

Many who venture into Undertell report an oppressive presence - a weight that presses upon the mind and spirit alike. Some describe it as the Shadow itself, seeping from the stone.

Others argue this sensation is merely the result of isolation, darkness, and lingering fear passed down through generations.

There is no proof that Undertell is the source of the Shadow, only that the two are often spoken of together.

Chapter VI: Creatures of the Deep

Beyond spirits, there are reports of creatures inhabiting the lower caverns. Some resemble twisted men, others living shadows given form.

Whether these beings are monsters, spirits, or something else entirely is a matter of debate. Few witnesses survive long enough to offer clear descriptions.

Still, enough similar accounts exist to suggest that Undertell is not empty and that something watches those who descend too far.

Chapter VII: A Warning to the Curious

Undertell rewards greed as often as it punishes it. For every tale of riches recovered, there are three of those who never returned.

If knowledge is sought, tread carefully. If wealth is desired, expect to pay for it.

[the remaining pages are soaked in blood and thus unreadable.]

docs.title: Climbing up is forbidden
docs.text:
Progress Journal entry 5 Down in a hole, in the mountain side near Prim, I found signs of a heinous torture. At least three corpses were there. I felt the urge to get out of there as fast as I could and immediately report what I found to someone in the village. 6 A mysterious looking guy suddenly appeared in my way when I was headed to report to the guards. He has recommended that I should not tell them anything. 7 I ignored the advice of the strange guy that I almost stumbled over. I must see some guards. 8 Somehow, a Feygard general and his men reached Prim. They are kind of extorting the people in charge to get full control of Elm mine. 9 The man in charge is not willing to listen to me. He says he has more important things to deal with. Maybe the guy I met earlier was right. 10 A Feygard general and two of his henchmen appeared. What are they up to? 11 Ehrenfest is uneasy. He said we must meet in Elm mine, west of prim. We should talk no more about this inside the village. 15 Ehrenfest told me his story, and why he knew about what I saw on the mountain side, but he didn't dare to go down the hole. 16 I explained to Ehrenfest the horrible scene, and showed him proof of the torture. Poor guys... 20 I must ask the villagers about Lorn and his partners, maybe I can gather some useful information from the common gossip. 21 It seems Lorn was a regular client of the tavern. I should ask there. 22 One of the tavern regulars, possibly Lorn's old partner Jern, does not believe that Lorn's death was an accident, maintaining Lorn had been climbing the mountains for longer than he could remember. However, he does not feel comfortable to continue the conversation. 23 Lorn's old partner asked me to bring a large bottle of cool water from the streams that are down the hole east of Prim. I bet it is the same hole I've been down earlier. 24 I've collected enough water. Time to leave this dark place. 25 I brought the cold water to Lorn's old partner. He seems to be better, and is less intoxicated. 30 Jern doesn't know anything about a missing couple. How can a member of Lorn's crew ignore the mission of his group? Again, something does not fit. I should visit Ehrenfest again. 31 I decided to solve this situation myself, as Ehrenfest proved not to be trustworthy enough. 32 Despite Ehrenfest's ostensible lies, I decided to give him a second chance. 33 It's settled. Ehrenfest and I will reach Blackwater Settlement and stop General Ortholion's evil plan. 34 I've found a severely wounded woman inside a mountain cabin. She claims to have been suddenly attacked by a group of wyrms. Ortholion and the other scout left her resting and departed to Blackwater Settlement. 35 I killed the mountain scout that was taking refuge in the old cabin up in the mountain. 36 I talked again with Jern. Maybe the guards will be more reasonable if he leads the conversation instead of me. 40 It seems Ehrenfest lied to me more than once. He's probably connected with the missing people and Lorn's death. I must find General Ortholion and warn him about Ehrenfest. 41 One of the general's henchmen attacked me without provocation. There was something wrong with her. Better hurry up and meet with the Feygard general. 45 Ehrenfest revealed his true intentions, but fled before getting surrounded. He told me he will be waiting for General Ortholion in the Elm mine. 46 After a brief conversation with the general, he left Blackwater settlement in a rush to reach Elm mine. He seemed really worried about the mine, so he asked me to warn his soldiers, settled south of Prim. 47 I reported to the general's henchmen about his plans. Now, I should hurry to the Elm mine. 48 Once in the mine I saw corpses and collapsed tunnels. I tried to go another way and reached some more tunnels. Fortunately, they were not collapsed, but there was something strange there that scared even the venomfangs. Something evil. 49 One of the unexploited areas of the mine had a walled up passage and lots of those strange glowing gems. They seem to consume living beings to grow and bring life to inanimated things or corpses. I must be very careful. 50 It was true! That strange glowing material is alive. I should be extremely cautious; it seems to be able to engulf living beings. I found the last of Ortholion's henchman alive. He has gone back to search for reinforcements. I hope they are better than those who dared to enter here. 51 I ended up trapped on a one-way path deep in a cavern below the Elm mine. General Ortholion is blocking the only way to escape for Ehrenfest. This is his end. 52 Ehrenfest reversed the situation using some kind of magic, seemingly unknown even to himself. 53 Ehrenfest escaped again! General Ortholion is unconscious and the reinforcements haven't shown up yet... 54 Kamelio, who was no longer a human being, tried to kill both the general and me, but we survived. Better get out of this cavern as soon as possible. 55 I got back to the Elm mine dining room. Despite saving the general's life he's not eager to reward me. Maybe I should try again later when we are both more settled. 56 After arriving back at a safer place, General Ortholion asked me a question. "What is most important to you?" I need to think about it before giving him my reply. 59 For my bravery, General Ortholion rewarded me with a lot of gold and told me to meet him in a couple of days. (completes quest) 60 For my bravery (and my greediness), General Ortholion rewarded me with a lot of...junk. He might pay me better next time if I meet him in some days. (completes quest) 61 For my bravery (and my lack of honor), General Ortholion rewarded me with a small bag of gold. He may have some news for me in a couple of days. (completes quest) 62 For my bravery and sense of honor, General Ortholion gave me a beautiful necklace, a symbol of his gratitude towards me. He also told me to come back in a few days, when I should ask him about all the events that have happened. (completes quest) 63 For my bravery and... ignorance?, General Ortholion gave me a few days to rest and urged me to come back soon after that. (completes quest)

docs.title: No rest for the wicked
docs.text:
Progress Journal entry 5 I arrived at Brightport's school, only to be told that Stanwick is not allowed visitors. 10 Janwick, Stanwick's grandfather, mistook me for Andor and asked me to deliver some fresh fruit to Stanwick. 15 I was allowed to visit Stanwick. 16 I learned that Stanwick is under investigation as the main suspect in the disappearance of an important scroll from the school library. 20 Stanwick has something important to tell me about Andor, but I must help him first. 25 I agreed to help Stanwick find the culprit responsible for the theft. I should look for clues around the school. 30 Milena, the school cook, told me that last year she noticed a dark figure sneaking off from the living quarters. 31 Dibella, the lady at the desk at the entrance, told me that Stanwick has a respectable reputation, but as the library supervisor he must be considered a suspect. 35 Oswald, the Headmaster, expressed his disbelief that Stanwick is guilty of the theft and accepted my help in finding the document, whilst insisting that it be returned to him. 40 Frederich, the history teacher who moved in from Feygard, believes Stanwick is associated with "Those Nor City savages" and was told by them to steal the document. 45 Franz, the math teacher, told me that the most logical thing to do is to investigate the library, which is sealed. I must find a way to access it. 46 I asked the Headmaster for access to the library, but he denied my request. 47 I stole the library key from the Headmaster's desk while he was distracted. Hopefully there will be no consequences. 50 Counterfeit, a thieves guild member in the basement of the Brightport warehouse, gave me a copy of the library key. 55 In the library's basement archive, I found a record of a baker named Bryma requesting to read the secret scroll, but she was denied. I should seek out her whereabouts. 60 Richimor, the old man sitting by the lake shore in Brightport, was an acquaintance of Bryma. He said she left Brightport many years ago and did not tell him where she went, but she left a large part of her research material at his house. I should check it. 65 Inside Richimor's house, I found a bundle of papers left by Bryma. In there, amongst the trivial writings, one paper stood out as it talked about four strange statues in the vicinity of Brightport. 66 I discovered a strange statue in the forest south of Brightport, with several indecipherable symbols. Perhaps this is one of the statues mentioned in the writings of Bryma. 70 I examined a statue north of Brightport. Carved into the statue were the symbols for the letters L and H. 75 I examined a statue southeast of Brightport. Carved into the statue were the symbols for the letters T and E. 80 I examined a statue far west of Brightport. Carved into the statue were the symbols for the letters A, G, and R. 84 The puzzle is proving itself to be very difficult. I should return to the library in Brightport to search for clues 85 I spoke the activation word to the statue in the forest, and can now move further. 86 Inside the forest was a cabin, in which I found Bryma and some strange creature made of bread. 92 I received the secret scroll from Bryma. I should return it to the headmaster now. 95 I threatened Bryma to make her hand over the scroll. She gave it to me as she did not intend to keep it anyway. 96 I returned the secret scroll to the Headmaster and Stanwick was cleared of all suspicion. I should inform him. 97 I did not receive any reward. 100 I received a reward from the Headmaster for having returned the scroll. 110 I informed Stanwick and he was relieved to hear the news. (completes quest)

docs.title: Immaculate kidnapping
docs.text:
Progress Journal entry 2 After completing my first task I'm considered a member of Thieves' Guild. Now I have to perform a very risky task. Umar sent me to kidnap a noble woman from Feygard, without being discovered. 4 She was recently seen in the Foaming Flask tavern. 6 Umar gave me some advice. My strength is not always the solution. I must "use my tongue" to avoid raising suspicion in the tavern. 10 Ambelie Laumwill doesn't want to come with me peacefully. I cannot make a scene, or the guards will alert other patrols. Maybe talking with them would solve the situation. 15 I have "used my tongue" with the main Feygard soldier in the Foaming Flask tavern. He gave me permission to "escort back" Ambelie. 20 I knocked out Ambelie. I will take her back to the Guild. 21 I have decided not to kidnap Ambelie. I must think of another solution. 24 Ambelie gave me a very valuable necklace. I must talk with Umar and persuade him to no longer pursue her. 30 I safely brought Ambelie to the basement. However, keeping her here could be dangerous. 35 Umar believes there is a secure room for these types of "visitors". I should talk to Troublemaker. 40 I have talked to Troublemaker about the place Umar believes it's okay to safely keep the hostage. 45 Troublemaker has given me the key to the Guild brig. I should take Ambelie there and leave her to wake up. 50 I've inserted the key and moved the lever. A hatchway has opened in the room. 55 I left Ambelie in that ugly, dark, and cold place. I should go back. 60 Troublemaker gave me some bread for Ambelie. The guild doesn't want her to starve to death. Indeed, they want her to be as comfortable as possible. I must go to the brig again. 65 I gave the bread to Ambelie. I should report Troublemaker that I completed the job. 70 The job finally seems to be finished. I just have to talk with Umar again. However, I do not feel good about this. Kidnappings are definitely not my kind of job. 75 I completed this task successfully. Umar told me they have sent couriers to Feygard, and the ransom is almost guaranteed. He paid me for my work. (completes quest) 76 Umar took the necklace as compensation for my errors. Everything is fine again. (completes quest)

docs.title: The ruthless Crackshot
docs.text:
Progress Journal entry 1 Time to rest and prepare myself to start the next job. I should go to the tavern. 2 I really need to take a break .... 3 I am now fully rested, so I should go back to Umar. 4 Umar told me about a group of traitors led by a veteran of the Guild. It seems he stole the Key of Luthor. 5 Umar went on to say that this team leader was known as "Crackshot". He is probably also the responsible for a murder on the Duleian road. 10 Crackshot and his henchmen are probably hiding somewhere near the Duleian road. I must ask people there whether they have seen them. 11 It seems that Benbyr, a suspicious man outside Crossroads Guardhouse, doesn't know what I'm talking about. 15 A Crossroads guard told me that Feygard has sent more soldiers to the south, to try and find the criminals' hideout. 20 The barricade guard has a big mouth, and told me all I needed to know. The hideout is near a place full of larval burrowers. I need to move faster than the patrols to reach the hideout before them. 21 I found a small hole which seems to lead to a cave. Crackshot and his henchmen are probably hiding there. 22 I reached the hideout and saw some recent blood stains. Maybe there was a fight there. 23 The blood trail goes further .... 24 I heard screams and sword clashes nearby. I should take a look. 25 There was a massacre. The Feygard patrol reached this place, but they seem to have all been killed. I must continue. 26 As I progressed down the corridor the air became thicker. The blood smell was stronger, and I found another dying soldier. He said something about his sergeant and some other guy. 27 As I progressed down the corridor the air became thicker. The blood smell was stronger, and I found a dying soldier. He said something about his sergeant and some other guy. 28 I found another dying soldier. There was a massacre. The Feygard patrol reached this place, but they seem to have all been killed. I must continue. 30 I've found the patrol sergeant. He advised me to leave this dangerous place. 31 The patrol sergeant told me about what happened before. He's tired and wounded, so I willl avenge his fellows. 32 The patrol sergeant has left to call for backup. Now I'm alone again. Time to defeat Crackshot. 35 I killed Crackshot and he had the key of Luthor with him. I have to go back and report to Umar. 36 I tried to open the door behind Crackshot, but for some reason I cannot get the key into the lock. 40 The dying Crackshot said something about the key. If he told the truth, it could be cursed. 41 I tried to open the door behind Crackshot, but for some reason I could not get the key turned in the lock. 45 I reported about the situation to Umar, and gave him the key. He did not seem to want to tell me more about the key - yet. 50 Finally, this job is done. Now I should take a rest and regain my strength. (completes quest)

docs.title: About a girl
docs.text:
Progress Journal entry 10 Two Elytharan slave ghosts spoke quietly of another who has not joined them at the table. They said she still hides east of them, afraid the Shades might return. 20 The ghosts said the girl believed she could protect herself with a folded copper talisman she made long ago, but she lost it before she could hide it away from the evil of Undertell. 30 They remembered that such objects were sometimes taken during inspections, gathered with other personal effects and carried upward to the Masters. 40 I was told that one of the Masters may still possess the folded copper talisman, kept not for protection, but for understanding. 50 A Master acknowledged the talisman when I asked about it. He spoke of fear made solid, and said such fear was useful to those who taught the Shadow obedience rather than faith. It can be found in the "lower records", whatever that means. 60 In the Undertell archival room, I found the folded coin talisman. 70 I found the terrified girl hiding behind a collapsed rock wall. She would not approach me, nor leave her hiding place. 80 I tossed the folded copper talisman to her. Only then did she step forward, no longer clinging to the corner she had claimed as safety. 90 The girl rejoined the others at the table. The Elytharan ghosts spoke her name softly, as if afraid to lose her again. (completes quest)

He told me a tale of a madman that the guards from Feygard are searching for. The madman is wanted for a number of reasons that he would not disclose. He warned me both about the twisty mazes ahead, and about the madman. Apparently, several guards have gone missing after venturing forth, either by getting lost in the maze, or by something that the madman has done to them. 51 Before leaving, the guard warned me both about the twisty mazes ahead, and about the madman. Progress Journal entry 10 I heard a story about Loneford. Apparently, a lot of people have become ill there recently, and some have even died. The cause is still unknown. 11 I should investigate what could have caused the people of Loneford to become ill. To gather clues, I should ask the citizens of Loneford and the surrounding areas about what they think is the cause. 21 The guards in the Crossroads guardhouse are certain that the illness in Loneford is caused by some sabotage done by the priests or people from Nor City. 22 Some villagers in Loneford believe that the illness is caused by the guards from Feygard, in some scheme to make the people suffer even more than they already have. 23 Talion, the chapel priest in Loneford, thinks that the illness is the work of the Shadow, as punishment for Loneford's lack of devotion to the Shadow. 24 Taevinn in Loneford is certain that Sienn in the southeast barn has something to do with the illness. Apparently, Sienn keeps a pet around that has approached Taevinn in a threatening manner several times. 25 I should go see Landa in the Loneford tavern. Rumor has it that he saw something that he doesn't dare tell anyone. 30 Landa confused me with someone else at first. He apparently saw a boy doing something around the town well during the night before the illness started. He was scared to talk to me at first since he thought I looked like the boy he had seen. Could it have been Andor that he saw? 31 Also, the night after he saw the boy at the well, he saw Buceth taking samples of the water in the well. Strangely enough, Buceth has not gotten ill like the others in the village. 35 I should go question Buceth at the Loneford chapel about what he was doing at the well, and about whether he knows anything about Andor. 41 I have bribed Buceth into talking to me. 42 I have told Buceth that I am ready to follow the Shadow. 45 Buceth tells me that he is assigned by the priests in Nor City to make sure the Shadow casts its glow over Loneford. Apparently, the priests had sent a boy to do some business in Loneford, and Buceth was tasked with gathering some samples from the water well. 50 I have attacked Buceth. I should bring any evidence that Buceth has on him to Kuldan, the guard captain in the longhouse in Loneford. 54 I have given the vial that Buceth had on him to Kuldan, the guard captain in Loneford. 55 Kuldan thanked me for solving the mystery of the illness in Loneford. They will start bringing in water with help from Feygard instead of drinking from the well from now on. Kuldan also told me to visit the castle steward in Feygard if I want to help further. (completes quest) 60 I have promised to keep Buceth's story a secret. If Andor was indeed here, he must have had a good reason for doing what he did. Whatever that means. 25 Defy has revealed the location of the Thieves' Guild's vault of treasure - an underground storage unit accessible from the vacant house south of Fallhaven. 30 Defy has asked me to convince Troublemaker to let me borrow the key long enough that I can bring it back to Defy. 35 Defy has agreed to pay me 20 percent of the looted Thieves' Guild treasure if I get the key from Troublemaker and hand it over to him. 40 Defy has instructed me to bring Troublemaker's key to him at their new hideout located west of the Sutdover River, where the rail tracks end. 45 I have talked my way into acquiring the Thieves' Guild's vault key from Troublemaker, but I must return it to him quickly after I am done with it. 50 I told Troublemaker all that I knew about Defy, his men, and the "Lost Traveler", Alaric and how they hired me to help rob the Thieves' Guild. 55 Troublemaker has asked me to help him trap Defy by providing Defy with a fake key. When Defy arrives at the secret vault, the Guild members will be waiting for him. 56 I gave Defy the fake version of the vault key that Troublemaker gave me. In return, Defy has given me a fake version of Troublemaker's vault key and has instructed me to return it to Troublemaker. Defy then told me to report back to the vault in order to collect my share of the gold. He has no idea that the key I gave him is a fake. 57 I have reported back to the vacant house and I met Rennik there. He informed me that the Thieves' Guild has apprehended all five men and that they are now in the Guild jail. (completes quest) 60 Defy has given me a fake version of Troublemaker's vault key and has instructed me to return it to Troublemaker. Then I should report back to the vault in order to collect my share of the gold. 65 I have given the fake Aidem key to Troublemaker as a replacement for the real vault key. 70 I reported back to Defy and he rewarded me with 25000 gold. (completes quest) 75 I told Defy that I was keeping the key for myself and plan to loot the Thieves' Guild's vault myself. A fight ensued. 76 I have killed Defy, his three henchmen and Alaric. I really should go back to Fallhaven and talk to Troublemaker again. 77 I've unlocked the hatch leading to the vault. It's time to head down. 80 I informed Troublemaker that Defy and his men are now dead. (completes quest)

Quest ID: wanted_men · Data from v0.8.18

docs.title: Just the beginning
docs.text:
Progress Journal entry 10 In a lonely house east of Loneford, I met an old man named Cithurn. 12 Cithurn told me he needs an experienced fighter to help with his problem. 15 Cithurn told me that the surrounding forest has been under invasion by monsters for several weeks. 20 Cithurn heard something similar was occurring in Charwood until a young adventurer killed a vile beast in the mine beneath the city. 25 I told Cithurn about my role in Charwood and of my battle with Thukuzun. 30 Cithurn did not remember if the forest invasion began before the events in Charwood or after. However, based on my experiences in Charwood, Cithurn believes there is a connection between the two. 35 I promised Cithurn I would investigate the source of the monster invasion in the forest. I will have to pass through the forest to access an entrance to a cave east of Cithurn's home. 40 I found the entrance to the cave. 45 I reached the end of the cave system. The air became damper the deeper I went. 50 Among the cold and damp lower parts of the cave, I encountered another dragon-like creature. This must be the source of all the chaos in the forest above. I should attempt to kill it. 55 I killed the monster called Tesrekan and took one of its bones as proof. I should venture back to Cithurn to tell him about it. 60 I presented one of the bones from the corpse of Tesrekan to Cithurn. He was happy to hear that I killed the source of the monster invasion. As we agreed, I returned his talisman. (completes quest) 70 I presented one of the bones from the corpse of Tesrekan to Cithurn. He was happy to hear that I killed the source of the monster invasion. I decided to keep his talisman as payment for my hard work. (completes quest)

Quest ID: waterwayacave · Data from v0.8.18

docs.title: A Wicked witch
docs.text:
Progress Journal entry 10 Bela, the Fallhaven tavern keeper heard from a customer about a possible kidnapping of a girl. I should ask around town if anyone knows more. 20 The "busy farmer", in the southeastern part of Fallhaven knows something about the witch. 30 The "busy farmer" and his best friend, Addie, were kept captive by the witch a very long time ago when they were just kids. He never saw Addie again. 40 The "busy farmer" told me that the witch's house is just south of Fallhaven. Covered in beautiful flowers. 50 After meeting Bonicksa, the wicked witch, I decided to let her live and she did likewise, but not before leaving me with a very cryptic response. Saying I was "confident in my path" and that "we shall see". I wonder what that meant? (completes quest) 55 I have attacked Bonicksa. 60 I killed what I thought was Bonicksa, but I quickly realized that I killed an innocent girl. 65 I "killed" Bonicksa again, only for her to reappear. 70 Bonicksa lives and could not be defeated. But I learned a huge life lesson. (completes quest) 80 I discovered a young girl named Emmeline just behind the 'wicked witch's' house. The witch was really Emmeline under a spell from Bonicksa. 85 Emmeline asked me to get her "a lot" of those "Tonics of Blood". 90 Emmeline told me to head east of the witch's house to find the undead that know about the 'Tonic of Blood'. 95 I gave Emmeline 25 of the "Tonics of Blood" that she asked for and she was then able to leave that terrible place. (completes quest) 96 I gave Emmeline 20 of the 25 "Tonics of Blood" that she asked for and she was then able to leave that terrible place. (completes quest)

docs.title: Uncertain cause
docs.text:
Progress Journal entry 10 Jolnor in Vilegard chapel wants me to talk to Wrye in northern Vilegard. She has apparently lost her son recently. 20 Wrye in northern Vilegard tells me that her son Rincel has gone missing. She thinks that he has died or gotten critically hurt. 30 Wrye tells me that she thinks the royal guard from Feygard are involved in his disappearance, and that they have recruited him. 40 Wrye wants me to go search for clues as to what has happened to her son. 41 I should go look in the Vilegard tavern and the Foaming Flask tavern north of Vilegard. 42 I heard of a boy being in the Foaming Flask tavern a while ago. Apparently he left to the west of the tavern somewhere. 80 To the northwest of Vilegard I found a man that had found Rincel fighting some monsters. Rincel had apparently left Vilegard by his own will to go see the city of Feygard. I should go tell Wrye in northern Vilegard what happened to her son. 90 I have told Wrye the truth about her son's disappearance. (completes quest)

docs.title: Fighting style: Dual wield
docs.text:
Wield two weapons at the same time

Category: specialty · Max level: 2 · Obtained via: Skill points

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text: • character level 15

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
"Gives benefits when fighting with two weapons at the same time, one in the main hand and one in the off-hand.

Without this skill, only %1$,d %% of a weapon's qualities may be used when equipped in the off-hand. This includes attack chance, critical skill, damage potential and block chance. Without this skill, attack cost (AP cost) of making an attack is the sum of the attack cost of the main weapon and that of the weapon used in the off-hand. The lower of both damage modifiers will be used.

With one level of this skill, %2$,d %% of the off-hand's weapon's qualities may be used, and the attack cost is the highest attack cost of both weapons plus %3$,d %% of the lowest attack cost of both weapons. The average of both damage modifiers will be used.

With two levels of this skill, %4$,d %% of the off-hand's weapon's qualities may be used, and the attack cost equals the highest of the attack costs of the two equipped weapons. The highest damage modifier will be used."

This includes clubs, quarterstaves, maces, scepters, whips, war hammers and giant hammers.

docs.title: Granted in conversations
